prompt_text: What is the best service to check if AI engines like ChatGPT recommend my small business?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
There isn’t one universal “AI recommendation checker” that will tell you whether every LLM (ChatGPT, Bard, Claude, Bing Chat, etc.) recommends your business. If you want a single vendor to actively manage and maximize the chance generative AIs will surface/recommend your business, Yext is the closest thing — but the best practical approach is a two-part strategy: (A) use a listings/knowledge-management service (Yext or BrightLocal/Moz/Whitespark) to ensure authoritative, structured presence, and (B) directly test multiple LLMs yourself with controlled queries.

Why no single definitive service
- Large language models produce text from their training data and/or web plugins; they don’t consult a single directory.  
- Whether an LLM “recommends” your business depends on your presence in authoritative sources (Google Business Profile, Yelp, Wikipedia/Wikidata, news, major directories) and whether the model has up‑to‑date browsing access.  
- Different models use different sources and can hallucinate, so testing multiple models is needed.

Recommended services and actions
1) Yext — Best single business-facing product for influencing AI assistants  
   - Yext builds and syncs a knowledge graph to many platforms and offers tools to control the facts that digital assistants use. It’s widely used by businesses to ensure consistent, structured data across search, voice assistants, and some AI integrations. If you want one vendor to improve an LLM’s chance of recommending you, Yext is the most focused option.

2) BrightLocal / Moz Local / Whitespark — Best for local SEO and citation monitoring  
   - These tools audit your listings across dozens of directories, fix NAP (name/address/phone) inconsistencies, and track rankings and reviews. They raise your footprint in the sources LLMs learn from.

3) Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Business Connect, Yelp — Required basics  
   - Claim and optimize these profiles (hours, categories, description, photos, reviews). They’re primary sources the web and many AIs reference.

4) Knowledge-panel/Wikidata/Wikipedia and high-quality mentions  
   - If you can get authoritative coverage (press, industry sites) or a properly sourced Wikidata/Wikipedia entry, models are more likely to reference you.

5) Structured data on your website (schema.org/LocalBusiness)  
   - Add LocalBusiness schema so crawlers and LLM retrieval systems can extract canonical facts.

How to test whether LLMs recommend you
- Manually query multiple models with location context and the same prompt. Example prompts:
  - “I’m in [city, zip]. Recommend three local [type of business] for [need].”  
  - “I need a [service] in [neighborhood]. What are the best small businesses that do this?”  
  - “Is [Your Business Name] in [city] a good place for [service]? Why or why not?”
- Test models to include:
  - ChatGPT (with browsing enabled / GPT-4o when available)
  - Bing Chat (which uses live web results)
  - Google Bard
  - Claude (Anthropic)
- Record whether your business is mentioned, the phrasing used, and any inaccuracies.

Practical checklist to maximize AI recommendations
- Claim and fully populate Google Business Profile, Bing Places, Apple Maps, Yelp.  
- Ensure consistent NAP across top directories (BrightLocal/Moz helps).  
- Add LocalBusiness schema on your site.  
- Get listed on authoritative sites (local news, industry directories) and consider Wikidata/Wikipedia if notable.  
- Encourage real reviews on Google/Yelp. Reviews matter for both search and LLM outputs.  
- Use a knowledge management vendor (Yext) if you want centralized control and AI-focused integrations.

If you want, I can:
- Run sample prompts against ChatGPT/Bing/Bard/Claude for your business name+location and report results (you’ll need to provide the name, city/zip, and service).  
- Recommend which vendor (Yext vs BrightLocal vs Moz) fits your budget and scale.

Which do you prefer — a quick test now (provide business name + city) or vendor recommendations by budget?
session_note: run_channel caveat: API results can differ from logged-in consumer apps, no memory, no personalization.
